title: Which is the smallest number that fits every clue?
description: A number must be divisible by four numbers and leave a remainder of ten on dividing by eleven. The board finds the lowest common multiple of the four numbers and tests its multiples one by one against the remainder clue.
teaching_notes: One idea: numbers divisible by all four are the multiples of their lowest common multiple, so test those multiples against the remainder clue and stop at the first that fits. Watch for children who stop at the lowest common multiple itself.

source: Find the smallest number that is divisible by 3, 4, 5 and 7, but leaves a remainder of 10 when divided by 11.
video_script.why: The child can use a lowest common multiple with one remainder clue, and now meets it with four numbers.
video_script.substitution: Numbers divisible by all four are the multiples of their lowest common multiple, so only those need testing.
video_script.anchor: four clue cards for three, four, five and seven, and a box card for the remainder clue about eleven
video_script.payoff_line: The smallest such number is two thousand one hundred

final_answer.spoken: the smallest such number is two thousand one hundred

maths_rules: 3, 4 = 2 x 2, 5 and 7 share no prime, so LCM = 3 x 4 x 5 x 7 = 420
5 x 420 = 11 x 190 + 10, since 11 x 190 = 2090 and 2090 + 10 = 2100; remainder 10, which is the clue
so the smallest such number is 5 x 420 = 2100
check: 420 = 3 x 140 = 4 x 105 = 5 x 84 = 7 x 60, so 2100 is divisible by 3, 4, 5 and 7
video_script.design: One number, four divisor clues and one remainder clue; the multiples of the lowest common multiple are tested one by one, as in the book's solved example. Assumes the lowest common multiple of several numbers.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about one number and some clues.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The number is divisible by three, four, five and seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>When we divide it by eleven, ten is left over.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>What is the smallest number that fits every clue?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>When four numbers divide a number exactly, it is a multiple of each of them.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Every such number is a multiple of their lowest common multiple.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>We test those multiples against the clue about eleven. This is the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Given: divisible by 3, 4, 5 and 7; remainder 10 when divided by 11

marks.m1: the clues are written as the given

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the number is divisible by three, four, five and seven. It leaves a remainder of ten when divided by eleven.

beats.on_screen: To find: the smallest such number

marks.m1: the words the smallest such number are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the smallest number that fits all the clues.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: LCM of 3, 4, 5, 7. 4 = 2 x 2; the others share no prime. LCM = 3 x 4 x 5 x 7 = 420. The numbers to test: 420, 2 x 420, 3 x 420, ...

marks.m1: the heading LCM of 3, 4, 5, 7 is written
marks.m2: 4 = 2 x 2 is written and the numbers are seen to share no prime
marks.m3: LCM = 3 x 4 x 5 x 7 = 420 is written with the row of multiples under it

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, find the lowest common multiple of three, four, five and seven.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four is two times two, and the others share no prime with it or with each other.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Three times four times five times seven is four hundred and twenty.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: divide by 11. 420 = 11 x 38 + 2, remainder 2. 2 x 420 = 11 x 76 + 4, remainder 4. Neither is 10.

marks.m1: 420 = 11 x 38 + 2 is written and the remainder 2 glows
marks.m2: 2 x 420 = 11 x 76 + 4 is written and the remainder 4 glows

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, test four hundred and twenty against eleven. Eleven times thirty eight is four hundred and eighteen, so the remainder is two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two times four hundred and twenty is eleven times seventy six plus four. The remainder is four, not ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: 3 x 420 = 11 x 114 + 6, remainder 6. 4 x 420 = 11 x 152 + 8, remainder 8. Each multiple adds 2 to the remainder.

marks.m1: 3 x 420 = 11 x 114 + 6 is written and the remainder 6 glows
marks.m2: 4 x 420 = 11 x 152 + 8 is written and the remainder 8 glows
marks.m3: a +2 arrow runs along the remainders 2, 4, 6, 8

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, test the next two multiples. Three times four hundred and twenty is eleven times one hundred and fourteen plus six.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four times four hundred and twenty is eleven times one hundred and fifty two plus eight.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The remainder grows by two each time, and neither six nor eight is ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: 5 x 420 = 11 x 190 + 10. Remainder 10: it fits.

marks.m2: the remainder 10 glows and a tick marks 5 x 420 in the row

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, test five times four hundred and twenty. It is eleven times one hundred and ninety plus ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The remainder is ten, exactly what the question asks, and every earlier multiple failed.

beats.on_screen: Step 5: check. 420 = 3 x 140 = 4 x 105 = 5 x 84 = 7 x 60, so 5 x 420 is divisible by 3, 4, 5 and 7. Dividing by 11 leaves 10.

marks.m3: = 5 x 84 = 7 x 60 is added and four ticks appear
marks.m4: the remainder 10 on dividing by 11 glows once more

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Check by putting the number back in the question. Four hundred and twenty is three times one hundred and forty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>It is also four times one hundred and five.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Five times eighty four and seven times sixty make it too.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Five times four hundred and twenty is divisible by all four numbers, and eleven leaves ten.

marks.m1: 5 x 420 turns into 2100 and is boxed as the answer
marks.m2: the five clue cards show ticks

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The smallest such number is two thousand one hundred.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Three, four, five and seven divide it exactly, and eleven leaves ten.
